rules.title: Maximum allowable rent increase for September 1, 2026 through August 31, 2027
rules.requirement: For September 1, 2026 through August 31, 2027, the maximum allowable annual rent increase is 2.87 percent.
rules.citation: Santa Ana Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
citation_aliases: Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: 2.87 percent is the maximum allowable rent increase for the period of September 1, 2026 through August 31, 2027.

effective_dates.quoted_span: for the period of September 1, 2026 through August 31, 2027

sunset_date.quoted_span: for the period of September 1, 2026 through August 31, 2027

rules.title: Annual rent increase cap: lesser of 3% or 80% of CPI
rules.requirement: Landlords may raise rent only once a year by an amount that does not exceed the lesser of 3% of current rent or 80% of the change in the Consumer Price Index.
rules.key_value: lesser of 3% or 80% of CPI change
rules.citation: Santa Ana Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
citation_aliases: Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: The increase cannot be more than 3% of your current rent or 80% of the Consumer Price Index (CPI) change, whichever is less.

rules.title: Just cause eviction requirement
rules.requirement: Landlords must have a valid reason to evict a tenant, such as nonpayment of rent, breach of the lease, or owner move-in. Some evictions may require relocation assistance for moving costs.
rules.citation: Santa Ana Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
citation_aliases: Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: Your landlord must have a valid reason to evict you. This could be for not paying rent, breaking the lease, or if the landlord wants to move into the property themselves.
